label: copy-phase input x (fed-back x, from the 3rd original position onward)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase when the fed-back input token is x, i.e. the model just output an x and now receives it as input (the x is original token recall_idx-1). It never fires during the original phase or on the delimiter, including on original-phase x inputs, and essentially never on any other input token. Magnitude grows with how late the x sits in the original sequence: x at original position 1 (recall_idx 2) gives weak activations (~0.02-0.2 of max), position 2 gives ~0.3-0.5, and x at later positions reaches 0.7-1.0. Some x inputs at original position 2 still do not fire. The output token, the previous token and the first token have no effect.

issues: No refuting evidence. Dev profile: 100% of activation mass is in the copy phase; original phase and delimiter have 0 active steps; phase0 & in_tok==x scores precision 0 and recall 0.
in_tok==x carries 1.000 of the mass. Other tokens fire on only 17 or fewer steps each (h 17, 1 8, f 8), which is scattered noise.

Position dependence holds. recall_idx 1 (x at original position 0) never fires. recall_idx 2 holds 0.9% of mass at a 0.5% rate, with weak 0.02-0.17 activations in the misses. recall_idx 3 holds 12.8% of mass over 15.6k active steps, while recall_idx 4 holds 23.6% over 13.9k, so mean magnitude rises after position 2 as claimed.

Test misses: 2703 steps (0.9% of mass), all weak x inputs at recall_idx 2 with no other systematic class. Test false positives: 575 steps, almost all x at original position 2 (recall_idx 3, precision 0.962 alone). recall_idx >= 4 alone has precision 0.99995. This is a mild soft edge at the cutoff, not a missing variable.
Reproduced the test scores: precision 0.990, recall 0.955, F1 0.972, mass recall 0.991. recall_idx >= 2 trades precision for recall and gets a lower F1 of 0.890, so the >= 3 cutoff is justified.
